reference_sql:
WITH campaign_clicks AS (  -- one row per campaign with spend in 2025
  SELECT ch.channel_name, c.campaign_id, SUM(a.clicks) AS clicks
  FROM ad_spend_daily a
  JOIN campaigns c ON c.campaign_id = a.campaign_id
  JOIN channels ch ON ch.channel_id = c.channel_id
  WHERE a.spend_date >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND a.spend_date < DATE '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY ch.channel_name, c.campaign_id
),
ranked AS (  -- one row per campaign with spend in 2025
  SELECT channel_name, campaign_id, clicks,
         RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY channel_name ORDER BY clicks DESC) AS rnk
  FROM campaign_clicks
)
SELECT channel_name, campaign_id, clicks
FROM ranked
WHERE rnk = 1

  SELECT ch.channel_name, c.campaign_id, SUM(a.clicks) AS clicks

  JOIN campaigns c ON c.campaign_id = a.campaign_id
  JOIN channels ch ON ch.channel_id = c.channel_id
  WHERE a.spend_date >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND a.spend_date < DATE '2026-01-01'

WHERE cc.clicks = (SELECT MAX(cc2.clicks) FROM campaign_clicks cc2 WHERE cc2.channel_name = cc.channel_name)

  GROUP BY ch.channel_name, c.campaign_id

SELECT cc.channel_name, cc.campaign_id, cc.clicks
FROM campaign_clicks cc
WHERE cc.clicks = (SELECT MAX(cc2.clicks) FROM campaign_clicks cc2 WHERE cc2.channel_name = cc.channel_name)
other_way.tradeoff: Comparing each campaign with its channel's highest clicks needs no window, and it keeps every tied campaign just as RANK does.

solver.query:
WITH p AS (SELECT ch.channel_name, c.campaign_id, SUM(a.clicks) AS clicks FROM ad_spend_daily a JOIN campaigns c ON c.campaign_id = a.campaign_id JOIN channels ch ON ch.channel_id = c.channel_id WHERE a.spend_date >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND spend_date < DATE '2026-01-01' GROUP BY ch.channel_name, c.campaign_id),
r AS (SELECT channel_name, campaign_id, clicks, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY channel_name ORDER BY clicks DESC) AS rn FROM p)
SELECT channel_name, campaign_id, clicks FROM r WHERE rn <= 1
